title: Weight Oracles: Reading Neural Network Weights with Language Models
read_level: full (arXiv PDF v1 via pdftotext: Secs 1-5, Appendices A-E; Figures 2-14 as captions only, so per-attack AUROCs in Fig 2 and transcripts in App. D not readable beyond text)
metadata_mismatch: Title/authors match (affiliation: University of Oxford; NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Neural Network Artifacts as a New Data Modality). Abstract wording differs from PDF v1: metadata says the external chain-of-computation 'delegates parameter-free operations to deterministic code' and the LLM 'learns to simulate the forward pass of small transformers from their weights'; PDF says it 'delegates composition to deterministic code' and the LLM 'learns the weight-reading primitive underlying the forward pass of small transformers, simulating them end-to-end'.
why_wsp: A fine-tuned Qwen 2.5 3B reads the raw weights of ~2K-parameter transformers, injected as projected continuous tokens with type embeddings, to simulate their forward pass (Phase I) and to answer diagnostic questions that flag unseen backdoors zero-shot (Phase II); no weight writing.
domain: Weight-space interpretability and backdoor detection on toy 1-layer transformers
editor: none (reader only): Qwen 2.5 3B-Instruct fine-tuned as explainer/oracle with a learned weight-row projection R^d -> R^2048 and type embeddings
target: 1-layer transformer (d=8, 2 heads, MLP dim 16, seq len 4, vocab 1000, 10 classes); "toy transformers of approximately 2K parameters" (Sec 5)
interface: other (weights as continuous embedded tokens into a trained LLM; Phase I uses external deterministic code for nonlinearities/composition, 5 LLM passes per target forward pass)
loop: n/a (Phase I: fixed 5-pass decomposition; Phase II: one-shot Q&A over 13 questions)

headline_results.quote: the decomposed chain-of-computation achieves 99.0% test accuracy on held-out real transformer models
It plateaued at exactly 45% and refused to budge.
accuracy plateaus at ~10% (chance) for ~2000 steps, then jumps to ~92% around step 2200
The oracle achieves AUROC = 0.93 +- 0.04 on the pos0-only cohort over five independent runs -- a 94% true positive rate at 20% false positive rate.
headline_results.where: Sec 4 Results (100 held-out models, 50 clean / 50 backdoored)

headline_results.quote: total L2 norm (null hypothesis) achieves AUROC 0.445, and the strongest V/O-pathway composite achieves 0.752

headline_results.where: Sec 4 Results; per-type in Fig 2 (figure only)

headline_results.quote: The oracle remains within 0.74–0.89 across all four types.
Initializing the oracle's weight-projection layers and type embeddings from the Phase I simulator checkpoint yields composite AUROC 0.73 against scratch's 0.81.

cost.quote: Phase II oracle training uses Adam, learning rate 1e-4, batch size 16, for 29,000 steps in bfloat16.
naive injection of full weight matrices into an LLM's context becomes computationally prohibitive beyond a few million parameters

baselines_and_controls: Hand-crafted weight-statistic detectors (total L2 norm; V/O-pathway composites); simulator-init vs scratch-init oracle; residual-only shortcut classifier (45.1%) as control for Phase I; type-embedding removal ablation; weight-matrix ablation. No comparison to a smaller non-LLM learned detector (stated as open).
runs_and_variance: "AUROC = 0.93 +- 0.04 on the pos0-only cohort over five independent runs" (Sec 4); other numbers single-reported.
robustness_of_edits: not tested (no edits); robustness to attacker adaptation tested via stealth (50x weaker) and adversarially regularized backdoors
memorization_vs_reasoning: Targets generated online so the reader "cannot memorise a fixed set of weights" (Sec 3; ~4,400 unique models in Phase II). Authors state the oracle "detects statistical correlates of backdoors rather than the backdoor mechanism itself" and "has learned a pathway-specific heuristic" (Sec 5). Phase I documented a shortcut (reading h, ignoring weights) at the 45% wall.
limitations_stated: Toy ~2K-parameter targets; scaling via context injection prohibitive beyond a few million parameters; detects correlates not mechanism (lastpos AUROC 0.74); 20% FPR at 94% TPR; narrow backdoor distribution (single-token triggers, single-class targets); natural-language interface not ablated against a smaller learned detector.
cites_or_builds_on: Diff Interpretation Tuning, Goel et al. 2510.05092
Huster et al. 2411.03445 (linear weight classification for trojans)
notes_for_survey: Precursor: posted 2026-10-05, about four weeks before the WSP term (2026-11-02), and does not use it; it is a B1 reading result but with a fine-tuned 3B LLM that ingests weights as learned continuous embeddings, unlike WSP's untrained frontier models reading weights via code/text. Later WSP work cites it as the trained weight-reader line (e.g. 2611.28781: "Language models have also been trained to read weights"). Results are on ~2K-parameter toy transformers only.
